raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60048. The docs for `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` differ from the code and from each other: one section claims a 4GB default while the code default is 0 (no override), and units flip between GB and GiB across pages.

## Claims

- docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.md: corrected to default 0 (no override), value in GiB, marked as legacy with a pointer to --kv-cache-memory-bytes
- docs/configuration/conserving_memory.md: same default/unit correction in the CPU backend bullet
- vllm/platforms/cpu.py: comment typo fix ("Lagecy" -> "Legacy")

## Validation

Verified against source on main: vllm/envs.py:52 (default 0) and vllm/platforms/cpu.py:307 (env var only applied when set, value multiplied by GiB_bytes, marked legacy). Docs build not run locally (Windows, no CUDA extensions), changes are single-line markdown edits, verified via git diff.

## Details

Root cause: the code default changed to 0 (legacy setting) but parts of the docs kept the old 4GB text, and GB/GiB usage drifted between pages.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -80,7 +80,7 @@ llm = LLM(model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct", enforce_eager=True)
 If you run out of CPU RAM, try the following options:
 
 - (Multi-modal models only) you can set the size of multi-modal cache by setting `mm_processor_cache_gb` engine argument (default 4 GiB).
-- (CPU backend only) you can set the size of KV cache using `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` environment variable (default 4 GiB).
+- (CPU backend only) you can set the size of KV cache using `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE` environment variable, in GiB (default 0, meaning vLLM doesn't override the KV cache size through this variable).
 
 ## Multi-modal input limits

@@ -293,7 +293,7 @@ See [AMD Zen optimizations](#amd-zen-optimizations) for detection rules, support
 
 ### How to decide `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`?
 
-This value is 4GB by default. Larger space can support more concurrent requests, longer context length. However, users should take care of memory capacity of each NUMA node. The memory usage of each TP rank is the sum of `weight shard size` and `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`, if it exceeds the capacity of a single NUMA node, the TP worker will be killed with `exitcode 9` due to out-of-memory.
+This value is 0 by default, which means vLLM doesn't override the KV cache size through this variable. When set, the value is in GiB (e.g, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`=40 means 40 GiB). Larger space can support more concurrent requests, longer context length. However, users should take care of memory capacity of each NUMA node. The memory usage of each TP rank is the sum of `weight shard size` and `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`, if it exceeds the capacity of a single NUMA node, the TP worker will be killed with `exitcode 9` due to out-of-memory. This is a legacy setting; use `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` instead.
 
 ### How to do performance tuning for vLLM CPU?

@@ -323,7 +323,7 @@ def check_and_update_config(cls, vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> None:
                     mamba_backend,
                 )
 
-        # Lagecy setting
+        # Legacy setting
         env_key = "VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE"
         if env_key in os.environ and os.environ[env_key] != "":
             kv_cache_space = int(os.environ[env_key])
